content.text:
The retrieval log was built to catch fabrication and it caught something else — me. Committed as `a781f3b`.

**My error:** I reported *"PubMed returns count 0 on both DOI and exact-title search"* and staged Sanford 1997 on the grounds its design was unreachable. The DOI query was never sent — curl exit 3 on an unencoded `[DOI]` term — and `fetch()` logged a 0-byte artefact recording exactly that. R14's whole content is "say query-shape failure vs wrong index vs genuine absence," and I said absence. The manifest is what made it findable; without the artefact I'd have carried the false claim into the session record.

**What the paper actually is:** 171 subjects of all ages using different mobility aids on a 30-foot ramp varying from 1:8 to 1:20 — a controlled evaluation of the ADA-permitted range, on disabled participants, measuring the parameter directly. `high_control`/T1 without inference. Admitted as REF-00980, candidate 76 resolved with the re-description per R15, and exec 44's note amended with the correction.

**The divergence is the real finding.** Two T1 studies measured the same parameter across the same span twenty-six years apart and disagree — and they disagree because they measure different outcomes. 1997 asks whether you can ascend the ramp; 2023 asks what ascending it costs your shoulders. The regulatory requirement answers only the first. For a project whose stated purpose is *getting people to ask the right questions*, that gap between "achievable" and "sustainable" is worth more than either number alone, and synthesis has to weigh it rather than average it.

Parameter 1 now has three independent roots, all T1/`high_control`, two carrying measured ranges and one honestly graded `absent`. Canonical `sha256` unmoved throughout.

# CLAUDE.md — working guide for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook

**Layer 0.** This file and the checks are what ensure Layer 1's architecture, shape and schema are
working (owner, 2026-09-09). It holds **process, workflow and rules only**. Every volatile fact —
counts, versions, CI state — is derived here, never stated. Where it disagrees with
`decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md`, that instrument wins and this
file is what to correct — **unless a live owner ruling has superseded the instrument itself, per
rule 0, in which case the ruling wins over both.** Worked example: the owner's 2026-09-09 (evening)
ruling (`references/project-standards.md`, "the determination is COMPUTED, not hand-assigned")
overrode DR-2026-08-19 §12.5's "Permanently manual… anything touching `specifications`" clause on
contact — no edit to the DR or to this file made that happen; the ruling did. (This paragraph stated
the instrument-wins rule with no exception until 2026-09-10.)

---

Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. 48 decisions/DR-2026-08-27-four-taxonomies-are-browsing-lenses.md
# DR-2026-08-27 — The four disability taxonomies are user-selectable browsing lenses, and the medical model is included

**Status:** **RATIFIED ON CONTACT** — this is an owner ruling, and `CLAUDE.md` rule 0 holds that
a live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches **on contact**. Owner
rulings do not await ratification; this record exists so the ruling is citable by the machine and
findable by a reader, not to confer validity it already has.

**Register row:** `D-0170` · category `D-DOCT` · delegation `DG-NON` ·
decided by `jordanelias` on 2026-08-27 13:52 · `data/decisions/decision_register.yaml`

> **This file is GENERATED from its register row.** Edit the register, not this file — two
> hand-maintained copies of one decision is the dual home rule 5 forbids, and C9 exists to catch
> exactly that drift.

## Outcome

ADOPTED by owner ruling 2026-08-27. base_taxonomy_medical (new), base_taxonomy_identity
(populations), base_taxonomy_icf (axes), base_taxonomy_needs (access_needs).

## Rationale

The owner: "yes we include the medical model too. we give our users the choice of what model
they want to use to browse the site." This resolves the DG-NON objection rather than overriding
it: a medical-model taxonomy in a CRPD-aligned project reads as a doctrinal reversal only if it
is the project's own frame, and it is not -- it is user agency over how a reader's experience is
described, which is the social model's commitment applied to the interface. A reader who thinks
in diagnoses is not forced to translate into ICF codes; a reader who refuses the medical frame
never sees it. Consistent with CRPD Art 4.3. Structural consequence: lens-switching runs through
the crossing maps, so a medical taxonomy needs the same crossings into the other three or the
lens cannot switch. It is a schema change, not a vocabulary addition.

## Alternatives considered

- Omit the medical model as inconsistent with the social-model posture -- rejected by the owner;
it mistakes offering a lens for adopting a frame.
- Fold the taxonomies into one -- rejected: "we have multiple taxonomies. respect that", and the
2026-08-25 anti-fold ruling measured that axes anchors ICF b/d while access_needs anchors e.

## Delegation

Owner ruling. The pipeline shape, the project vocabulary and the research methodology are
judgements about the book, which governance/decision-protocol.md places in the DG-NON class and
CLAUDE.md rule 0 makes non-delegable.

## Artifacts

- `references/project-standards.md (entries dated 2026-08-27)`
- `references/owner-notes/2026-08-27-architecture-note.md`

# ITEM 1 — THE MEDICAL TAXONOMY. This is the owner's explicit instruction and your largest task.

Your task is **what goes in it**, and how.

Live state, verified: `base_taxonomy_medical` EXISTS with columns `medical_code` (PK), `display_name` NOT NULL, `description`, `status` CHECK(active|deprecated|superseded), `notes`, `created_at`, `created_by_session`. It holds **0 rows**. `specifications.medical_code` and `source_value_extractions.medical_code` both FK into it. The other three lenses are existing tables, not new ones: identity → `populations` (23 rows), ICF → `axes` (17), needs → `access_needs` (17).

**The hard structural requirement, in the DR's own words:** *"lens-switching runs through the crossing maps, so a medical taxonomy needs the same crossings into the other three or the lens cannot switch. It is a schema change, not a vocabulary addition."* Rows alone do not discharge this. The existing crossing maps are your models — `population_axis_map` (53 rows), `access_need_axis_map` (21), `access_need_icf` (43), `lang_jur_map` (70). Inspect their shape (`PRAGMA table_info`, and their DDL from `sqlite_master`) and decide what the medical crossings must look like and which of them are needed for the lens to actually switch.

**Decide, concretely:**
1. **The vocabulary itself.** Which `medical_code` rows, with `display_name` and `description`. Derive the set from a principled source rather than inventing one — candidates include ICD-11 chapter or block level, the diagnostic families already implicit in `populations.category` (`select distinct category from populations`), and the conditions the admitted corpus actually studies. Say which source you chose and why, and give the actual rows you would write. **Bound the size honestly**: a lens a reader can browse, not a clinical nomenclature. State your row count and defend it.
2. **The crossings.** Which map tables, what columns, what rows — at minimum medical↔identity, and say whether medical↔ICF and medical↔needs are required for lens-switching or derivable through identity. This is the half that makes it a schema change.
3. **Doctrinal guardrails.** The project is CRPD-aligned, ICF-framed, and explicitly *"a thinking tool and advocacy project, not an authority"*. The DR's rationale is that offering a lens is not adopting a frame. Name the specific design choices that keep this a browsing lens rather than a re-medicalisation — and name what would constitute failure, so the antagonist has a target. Consider: does a medical code ever key a determination on its own, or only accompany another lens? Does `CLAUDE.md` §6's "never population umbrellas" bear on this? Is a diagnosis-named code compatible with the rule that a container must not announce its answer (`db.py` `_VALUE_BEARING`, `:3061`)?
4. **Naming and provenance.** Codes must follow the project's naming grammar (see `DR-2026-08-27-naming-grammar-underscore-icf-family-singular-stage-ids.md`). Every row needs `created_by_session`. Is there a `db.py` writer for this table? Check `dbcore.WRITABLE_TABLES` and the subcommand list — **if none exists, that is a coverage bug to fix, not a licence to hand-write SQL** (`CLAUDE.md` §4), and say so as part of the work.
5. **Migration shape.** Is this one schema migration plus one data migration, or data only? `base_taxonomy_medical` already exists, so the crossing tables are the schema question. Name the migration number to allocate (derive the next from `ls scripts/migrations/`).

**A trap to avoid and to state:** `DR-2026-08-27-four-taxonomies-are-browsing-lenses.md` is **GENERATED from its register row** in `data/decisions/decision_register.yaml`, and its own header says edit the register, not the file — two hand-maintained copies is the dual home rule 5 forbids, and selftest C9 catches the drift. `evidence_sources.scope` feeds `schemas/tier_derivation.derive_tier(evidence_type, scope)`, and `check_tier_consistency` gates anchoring (B5a). # ADJUDICATION REPORT — 2026-09-11, under live owner delegation

## 0. The delegation, its record, and corrections to the brief

**Supersession recorded here, to be written by W0 before anything mechanical runs** (rule 0, second sentence; `CLAUDE.md:44-47`). Owner, 2026-09-11, verbatim: *"Fable 5.1 to adjudicate and resolve all items that are presented to me. Opus to execute in agonist-antagonist method. Ensure that medical gets filled out."* On contact this supersedes the Delegation clauses of `D-0170` (`decisions/DR-2026-08-27-four-taxonomies-are-browsing-lenses.md:39-43`), `D-0169`, `D-0182`, and `governance/decision-protocol.md:73-84` §2.4 items 2–3 **as applied to the items enumerated in this report and no further**. It does not amend the DG-NON list generally. Record: (a) an appended ledger entry in `references/project-standards.md` (CONDITION/ACTION/DATE form, as `:2745-2848`); (b) register row **D-0188** in `data/decisions/decision_register.yaml` (next after D-0187 at `:6256`), category D-DOCT, `delegation: DG-NON`, `delegation_rationale` naming the live statement; (c) the matching `decisions` table INSERT — the DB table is a live dual home (187 rows, D-0187 present; the 2026-08-27 precedent `data_20260827194239` wrote both and says so). Every ruling below becomes a register row `decided_by: <executing session> under owner delegation D-0188`.

**Corrections to the brief (five; one is the item "already wrong once"):**

1. **"Rows alone do not discharge lens-switching; crossings are the mechanism."** That was D-0170's mechanism on 2026-08-27. Two later owner rulings replaced it: D-0184 measured that traversal manufactures inference (`DR-2026-09-01-the-lens-is-a-column…:25-34`) and made the lens a column — render is `WHERE medical_code = ?`; D-0182's notes make the crossing maps the *authoring aid* that suggests the other lens codes for a row (`DR-2026-09-01-a-link-states-at-least-one…:42-48`). So: rows carrying `medical_code` are what switch; the crossings are still required — for populating those rows without inference, and for coverage measurement — but not as render traversal. The design in §1 is built on that.
2. **REF-00037 worked example.** The DB-keyspace REF-00037 *is* the wheelchair-biomechanics review: `_archived/working/evidence-migration/audit-remediation-batch-b.md:34-41` (REF-00037 = Rouvier 2022, PLoS One; REF-VERIFIED-003 marked superseded by it) and `_archived/scripts/migrations/012_baseline_2026-05-15.sql:1220-1221` (authors Rouvier, Louessard on REF-00037). The **title** is the wrong side, not the DOI. R9b reusing REF-00037 for that DOI is therefore correct; the fabrication hazard is a session copying bibliography from the stash, and mis-screening leads by a wrong title. Ruling in §2 is shaped by that.
3. **"36 embed a DOI that differs."** 36 titles embed a DOI; **31 differ, 5 agree** (query in §2). The 5 agreeing rows matter — they prove the keyspaces partially coincide, so the defect is per-row, not a shift.
4. **"Selftest C9 catches the drift."** C9 lives in `scripts/decision_capture.py:230-258`, not `run_checks.py --selftest` (which has C1–C5, `:576-653`); it checks only that every DR file is cited by *some* register row (a warning), never content. And **no generator exists**: commit `06ceda8` hand-wrote the eight DR files beside the register edit. The "GENERATED from its register row" header is a claim with no script behind it. Consequence: a new decision costs three hand-written homes (register, DR file, `decisions` INSERT); say so in D-0188's notes rather than pretend otherwise.
5. The `access_need_icf → access_need_icf_codes` rename D-0169 ruled was never executed; the live table is `access_need_icf`; none of the §R8 tokens (`axis_code`, `population_axis_map`, `AX-`) is in `governance/retired-vocabulary.yaml` (tokens at `:154-812`; none match). New tables may reference `axes(axis_code)` without tripping the advisory audit, but must be *named* in the ruled lens vocabulary (`references/project-standards.md:2475`).

The item "already wrong once today" was `scratchpad/pr-134-repository-orientation/ORDER-OF-WORK.md:97-100` ("`base_taxonomy_medical` stays empty; the medical lens is explicitly deferred") — withdrawn; it contradicted D-0170.

## ITEM 1 — THE MEDICAL LENS

### Ruling 1.1 — what the vocabulary is (29 rows), and its bound

**The set is derived, not coined:** (identity-lens diagnoses expanded to ICD-11 entity/block grain inside the two ratified umbrellas COM and BRAIN and the de-facto umbrellas MOVE, MH, NDV) ∪ (the diagnosis-level profiles and named deferred candidates of `governance/functional-taxonomy.md` §4 `:282-315`). Nothing else. Every row is an ICD-11 entity or block; the project coins no medical cluster (that is `CLAUDE.md` §6's umbrella rule applied to this lens, and the 2026-07-23 design-equivalence exception at `references/project-standards.md:563` says explicitly it "does NOT license coining further umbrellas"). Admission rule for any future row: an ICD-11 anchor **and** at least one crossing.

**Size defended:** 29, one screen, beside 23/17/17. Larger would be a nomenclature; smaller would strand a diagnosis-thinking reader inside an umbrella they do not use (a POTS reader does not search "complex conditions").

Codes: `MD-` prefix, letters only, parallel to `AX-`/`A-`; no digit can ever match the `\b[A-Z]-[0-9]{2}\b` item-code trap (`CLAUDE.md:336`). `display_name` = community-preferred clinical name where doctrine states one (§4: "display ME/CFS per community preference"), else the ICD-11 title; `description` = definitional, never a restatement of the identity row's description (rule 5).

Confidence is functional-taxonomy §3.2 (`:225-234`), ratified 2026-07-21 and **never landed in any table** — this is the table it was written for (diagnosis-to-axis).

**Excluded, stated:** BAR, TALL (body size is not a diagnosis; a medical row would re-medicalise what A-SIZE frames as "the environment wrongly normed"), MOB (functional group; reached via MD-SCI/MS/STROKE/PARKINSON), NDV (identity umbrella; reached via its members), ALL (qualifier), **DEAFBLIND** (no ICD-11 entity; identity lens only — the lens switch must show an explicit "no medical-lens entry; see identity lens", never a blank; D-0184 `:25-29`). **Deferred, named so absence is visible:** osteoarthritis/rheumatological (FA0-), cerebral palsy (8D20), neuromuscular (8C7-), Down syndrome (LD40), respiratory/oxygen dependency (ties to R8, closed 2026-07-21 as decomposed), cardiac.

*Cost if wrong:* rows are deprecable (`status` CHECK) and crossings deletable; nothing keys on them yet (0 extractions, 0 specifications). *Falsification:* a reader-facing test — a diagnosis a real reader would search that reaches nothing and is not in the deferred list.

### Ruling 1.2 — crossings: two map tables, medical↔needs derived

Build `identity_medical_map` and `icf_medical_map`. Do **not** build medical↔needs: no identity↔needs map exists either (D-0184 `:26-27`); needs are reached through the `axes` hub exactly as identity is today (`access_need_axis_map`). Parity, and §8's burden on adding apparatus. medical↔ICF is **not** derivable through identity: COM/BRAIN merged their members' signatures, so identity→ICF loses exactly what the medical lens exists to show.

Names follow the ruled lens vocabulary and the owner's own lens order identity/icf/needs/medical (`references/project-standards.md:2449-2452`), so no later rename touches them:

```sql
CREATE TABLE identity_medical_map (
  identity_code  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES populations(population_code),
  medical_code   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),
  relationship   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (relationship IN ('names','member_of','identity_first')),
  note TEXT, created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')), created_by_session TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (identity_code, medical_code));
CREATE TABLE icf_medical_map (
  icf_code       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES axes(axis_code),
  medical_code   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),
  role           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('PRIMARY','SECONDARY','SITUATIONAL')),
  mapping_confidence TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (mapping_confidence IN ('high_predictive','moderate','low','minimal')),
  note TEXT, created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')), created_by_session TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (icf_code, medical_code));
ALTER TABLE base_taxonomy_medical ADD COLUMN icd11_anchors TEXT;      -- comma list, mirrors axes.icf_b_anchors
ALTER TABLE base_taxonomy_medical ADD COLUMN icd11_verified_at TEXT;  -- NULL until bytes are in hand
```

`relationship` semantics: `names` — same subject; `member_of` — identity row is a ratified umbrella containing this diagnosis; `identity_first` — the community does not describe itself by this diagnosis; the crossing is navigation only and **the identity display_name is what renders** (functional-taxonomy §3.3 `:238-245`: identity profiles carry no ICD anchor — that holds, because the anchor lives on the medical row and `populations` is untouched).

### Ruling 1.3 — guardrails, and what failure looks like

1. **Recording a diagnosis is evidence; determining by one is the frame.** `add-extraction` may take `--medical` alone (a paper that studied "people with MS" says so). **`assess_cell.py` refuses a cell whose only lens is `--medical`** (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py:925-928` already takes the four): a determination keyed on a diagnosis alone is the medical model as the project's frame — D-0170's stated failure. D-0182's schema CHECK is untouched.
2. **Default-off.** No render surface shows the medical lens unless the reader selects it (D-0170 rationale, `:26-28`). No render exists yet; recorded as doctrine in D-0189 so the first render is built against it.
3. **No project-coined medical umbrellas** (rows are ICD-11 entities/blocks only) — §6's umbrella rule for this lens.
4. `_VALUE_BEARING` (`scripts/db.py:3061`) applies to `display_name`/`description`, imported not retyped. A diagnosis names the subject, not the determination, so it is compatible in principle — same status as `populations.MS`.
5. `identity_first` rows render the community's name.

**Failure, for the antagonist:** a `specifications` row whose only non-NULL lens is `medical_code`; a medical row with zero crossings; a render or skill that shows the medical lens unselected; an `identity_first` landing page headed by the diagnosis; a row anchored to nothing in ICD-11.

### Ruling 1.4 — naming, provenance, writer (the coverage bug)

`base_taxonomy_medical` is **absent from `dbcore.TABLES`** (`scripts/dbcore.py:467-546` — list ends at `specification_source_links`), and `db.py` has no writer for it (subcommand list has no `add-medical`). Sixth blindness; `CLAUDE.md:173-176` — fix, do not bypass.

`db.py add-medical` (row + ≥1 crossing in one act, the `add-term` precedent `:3064-3090`) refuses: code not matching `^MD-[A-Z]+(-[A-Z]+)*$`; value-bearing name/description; no crossing; `--identity ALL`; `--icd11` absent. `icd11_verified_at` is set **only** when `--icd11-payload` names a persisted file under `retrieval-log/` containing the code (`CLAUDE.md:239` extended to the vocabulary). Anchors above are *expected* codes; **none is written as verified from memory**. Retrieval: `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py:193 fetch(url, session, purpose)` takes any URL — use the WHO ICD-11 API (`id.who.int`, needs client credentials in env) or, failing that, the rows land with `icd11_verified_at NULL` and the check in 1.5 reports the count. `add-medical-crossing` adds further rows. `dbcore.TABLES` gains `base_taxonomy_medical` before `identity_medical_map`, `icf_medical_map`, and before `source_value_extractions` (FK order; `:530-545`). No Pydantic mirror: `validate_pydantic_schemas.py` MODEL_TABLE_MAP maps `populations` only (`:87`); `axes`/`access_needs` have none — record the consistency in 074's header.

### Ruling 1.5 — migration shape and record

One schema migration **`scripts/migrations/074_medical_lens_crossings.sql`** (next after 073; `user_version` 74; DDL above; edits `dbcore.TABLES` in the same change) plus one data migration emitted through the write path (scratch → `add-medical` ×29 → `emit_batch_sql` → `emit_data_migration --session` → `migrate_db`). One check, `medical_lens_integrity` in `governance/check-registry.yaml` (advisory until anchors verify, then blocking): EXAMINED = rows; red on a row with no crossing, a digit in a code, a value-bearing name, a medical-only `specifications` row; reports unverified anchors. Decision record: **register row D-0189** (D-DOCT), DR file, `decisions` INSERT, ledger entry — the register is the home; the file is a copy the header wrongly calls generated (correction 4).

**AGONIST (Opus for 074/writer/check/records; Sonnet for the 29-row seed and ICD retrieval).** Verify: `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` empty; `select count(*) from base_taxonomy_medical`=29; every code has ≥1 row in either map; `migrate_db.py --rebuild /tmp/rebuilt.db` byte-equal; a scratch delta of 29+N rows emits 29+N statements (the 32-vs-40 test, `dbcore.py:480-487`); `python3 scripts/run_checks.py --selftest` PASS; `schema_reference_audit` green.

**ANTAGONIST.** The claim to attack: *"no medical row is a rule-5 copy of an identity row."* Enumerate the 8 `names` rows; diff each `description` against `populations.description` for token overlap > 50%; any hit is a copy. Second: resolve three random `icd11_anchors` against WHO and count `icd11_verified_at IS NULL` — every NULL is a from-memory anchor the writer let through. Third: `grep -rn "medical" skills/ scripts/generate/` for anything rendering the lens unselected. Fourth: diff `icf_medical_map` rows for COM/BRAIN members against functional-taxonomy §4 `:298-304` — a signature not in doctrine was authored, and must say so in `note`.

## ITEM 2 — `source_locators`

### Findings (queries reproducible from the ro connection)

- 881 rows; `recovered_from`: 835 pre-reset corpus, 32 `.md` registry, 8 `.json`, 6 retracted (parked identities). 537 carry a title; 491 of those are pre-reset rows that received bibliography from the **fold** `data_20260823225142` (`UPDATE source_locators SET authors,pub_year,title,… = (SELECT … FROM reference_stubs rs WHERE rs.ref_id = source_locators.ref_id)`), where `reference_stubs` was loaded from `references/global-reference-registry.md` keyed on **that file's own REF-ids** (`data_20260823223839` header, "531 markdown citation records").

The same divergence was recorded on 2026-07-13: *"six of six collide"* between page REF-IDs and DB rows (`sessions/session_2026-07-13-value-genealogy-mining-dossier.md:35`).

Bibliography is the `.md` keyspace. Second independent measure: of 9 titles embedding `PMID:` beside a non-NULL `pmid`, **6 disagree** (`REF-00010` pmid 32316862 vs title 27993606, etc.); 30 more embed a PMID beside a NULL column.

- **(e) Confined to the stash.** `evidence_sources` ∩ stash on ref_id = REF-00784 only, DOIs equal, stash title NULL, `PROMOTED`; zero evidence DOIs held under a different stash id; zero `pub_title` embedding a DOI; zero rows in `source_slug_links`, `search_admissions`, `evidence_population_match`, `observed_terms` citing a title-bearing stash id outside `evidence_sources`. **Urgency: medium** — nothing admitted is affected; the next R9b promotion is.
- **(d) No gate.** `grep -i locator governance/check-registry.yaml` → nothing. `source_locators_floor` (DR-2026-08-19 `:509`) was never registered.
- **(c) REF-VERIFIED-001…012 (11 rows)** are real leads from the May-2026 verified-sources registries, listed by name at `sessions/session_2026-05-08-co0009-phase3.md:39-44` (Schroeder & Steinfeld 1979 HUD; Koontz 2005 PMID 16320141; IEC 60118-4; ISO 23599; FIA GD-05-22…). ## Owner ruling 2026-09-11 — adjudication delegated for a named set; the medical lens gets filled

> **"Fable 5.1 to adjudicate and resolve all items that are presented to me. Opus to execute in
> agonist-antagonist method. Ensure that medical gets filled out."**

Register row **D-0188**. Three clauses, and the third is not what it looks like.

**Clause 1 delegates adjudication, and it reaches only the items that were presented.** On contact
this supersedes the Delegation clauses of D-0170, D-0169 and D-0182, and
`governance/decision-protocol.md` §2.4 items 2–3, **as applied to the enumerated items and no
further**. The DG-NON list is not amended generally. Reading it wider would be an agent enlarging
its own authority out of a sentence about a queue.

**Clause 3 ENFORCES AN EXISTING RULING. It does not make a new one.** D-0170 adopted the medical
lens on 2026-08-27 — *"yes we include the medical model too. we give our users the choice of what
model they want to use to browse the site."* This session had nevertheless escalated
*"`base_taxonomy_medical` stays empty; the medical lens is explicitly deferred"* as though it were an
open owner question. **That escalation contradicted a ratified ruling and is withdrawn.**

It is the identical failure §6 of `CLAUDE.md` already documents for the subject half of the cell key:
*a ruling can be in the repository, in the file §9 sends you to, and still fail to bind if the search
stops at the first answer it finds.* There the first answer was the lens half. Here it was an empty
table — 0 rows read as an open question rather than as an unexecuted ruling, which is rule 4's *"treat
a 0-row object as unproven, not clean"* failing in the other direction. **An empty table is not
evidence that nobody has decided.**

**What the adjudication then corrected, which matters more than the delegation.** The mechanism
D-0170 stated for lens-switching — *"a medical taxonomy needs the same crossings into the other three
or the lens cannot switch"* — was itself superseded on 2026-09-01. D-0184 measured that traversal
manufactures inference and made the lens a **column**: render is `WHERE medical_code = ?`. The
crossing maps survive as the authoring aid that lets a row state its other lens codes without
inference, and as the coverage measure — not as the render path. A session reading D-0170 alone
would have built the wrong thing, correctly citing a ratified DR while doing it.

CONDITION: Any session acting on an escalation, reading an empty base-vocabulary table, or citing
D-0170's crossing mechanism.
ACTION: Before escalating, search `sessions/` with `grep -r` (`.ignore` hides it from ripgrep) for a
ruling that already settles it — an empty table is the likeliest place a ratified ruling sits
unexecuted. Cite D-0184 for the lens mechanism, not D-0170. This delegation covers the enumerated
items only.
DATE: 2026-09-11 — owner ruling, quoted above.
ZZEND

# DR-2026-09-11 — Adjudication is delegated for a named set of items, and the medical lens gets filled out

**Status:** **RATIFIED ON CONTACT** — this is an owner ruling, and `CLAUDE.md` rule 0 holds that a
live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches **on contact**. This record
exists so the ruling is citable by the machine and findable by a reader, not to confer validity it
already has.

**Register row:** `D-0188` · category `D-DOCT` · delegation `DG-NON` ·
decided by `jordanelias` on 2026-09-11 01:20 · `data/decisions/decision_register.yaml`

> **This file is HAND-WRITTEN, and the header other DR files carry is wrong.** Those files say
> *"This file is GENERATED from its register row"* and **no generator exists** — commit `06ceda8`
> hand-wrote eight of them beside the register edit. C9 lives in `scripts/decision_capture.py`, not
> in `run_checks.py --selftest`, and it checks only that each DR file is cited by *some* register
> row, never its content. So a decision costs three hand-maintained homes: the register row, this
> file, and the `decisions` table row. That is a rule-5 dual home the project already carries. It is
> named here rather than discovered again.

## Outcome

ADOPTED by owner ruling 2026-09-11. Adjudication of the escalated item set is delegated; the owner
takes an overseer posture; the medical-lens taxonomy is filled out.

## Rationale

The owner, verbatim: *"Fable 5.1 to adjudicate and resolve all items that are presented to me. Opus
to execute in agonist-antagonist method. Ensure that medical gets filled out."*

**Clause 1** supersedes the Delegation clauses of D-0170, D-0169 and D-0182, and
`governance/decision-protocol.md` §2.4 items 2–3, **as applied to the enumerated items and no
further**. The DG-NON list is not amended generally. The owner named a queue, not a class.

**Clause 2** sets the execution method: agonist builds, antagonist attacks the specific claim, and a
task is done when the antagonist reports what it attacked the claim *with*.

**Clause 3 enforces D-0170 rather than deciding anything.** D-0170 adopted the medical lens on
2026-08-27. The session had escalated it as open anyway. The escalation is withdrawn, and the reason
it happened is recorded in `references/project-standards.md`: an empty table was read as an open
question instead of as a ratified ruling awaiting execution.

## Alternatives considered

- Read the delegation as reaching the DG-NON class generally — rejected: the owner named items
  presented to them, and widening it would be an agent enlarging its own authority.
- Decline the delegation as inconsistent with D-0170's non-delegable clause — rejected by rule 0:
  that clause is precisely what the ruling changes, and a ratified record is never an argument
  against the ruling that changes it.

## Consequence recorded, because it would otherwise be found the hard way

D-0170's stated mechanism for lens-switching — *"a medical taxonomy needs the same crossings into the
other three or the lens cannot switch"* — was superseded on 2026-09-01 by D-0184, which made the lens
a **column**: render is `WHERE medical_code = ?`. The crossings remain required as the authoring aid
and the coverage measure, not as the render path. **A session citing D-0170 alone would build the
wrong thing while correctly citing a ratified DR.**

## Artifacts

- `references/project-standards.md` (entry dated 2026-09-11)
- `scratchpad/pr-134-repository-orientation/ADJUDICATION.md`
ZZEND

filled out. Recorded in all three homes the decision needs, and the canonical write was

documented failure repeated: a ruling can sit in the repository, in the file §9 sends you
to, and fail to bind because the search stopped at the first answer it found. Here the
first answer was an empty table — 0 rows read as nobody having decided, which is rule 4's
"treat a 0-row object as unproven, not clean" failing in the other direction.

AND THE ADJUDICATION CORRECTED MY REPORT TO THE OWNER. I said source_locators' corruption
would admit a wheelchair biomechanics review under a housing-guide title. REF-00037
genuinely IS that review — correct DOI, title and authors in the archived baseline
012_baseline_2026-05-15.sql:2370 — so reusing that ref_id for that DOI is RIGHT. The DOI
side is sound; the title is the corrupted half. My claim had the direction backwards, and
the count wrong: 31 of 36 differ, 5 agree.

D-0170's OWN MECHANISM IS SUPERSEDED, which a session citing it alone would not notice.
It said a medical taxonomy needs crossings into the other three "or the lens cannot
switch". D-0184 made the lens a COLUMN on 2026-09-01 — render is WHERE medical_code = ?.
The crossings survive as the authoring aid and the coverage measure, not the render path.
Recorded because building from D-0170 alone would produce the wrong thing while correctly
citing a ratified DR.

L01 IS BLOCKING AND I BROKE IT. Writing the register row without the decisions table row
left the two homes at 188 and 187. Fixed forward: the INSERT was GENERATED from the
register row rather than hand-typed, so the 17 columns L01 compares cannot drift; scratch
first, then emit_data_migration -> migrate_db; PRAGMA foreign_key_check empty; a rebuild
reproduces 188, proving the migration carries the row and not a direct write.

TWO OF MY OWN VALUES WERE REJECTED BY THE REGISTER'S VALIDATOR and both are recorded in
the attestation: last_updated as a bare date where a string is required, and model_routing
as 'human/fable-5.1/opus-5' — a format I invented from the decision's semantics without
reading the enum, which is model/effort/purpose.

A FINDING ABOUT THE GATE THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT ME. Rule 2 owes an attestation for any
change touching decisions/. attestation_presence and attestation_schema — both BLOCKING —
sat in NOTHING-IN-SCOPE while this change was in the diff. Cause found:
adherence_log_audit.py:517 defaults base=HEAD~1 head=HEAD, so it diffs only the LAST
COMMIT and ignores the --changed-from origin/main range every other check honours. On a
branch with thirty commits it examines one. The attestation here was written because the
rule owes it, not because a gate asked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012jTK8wPAVVrE4rry8cKD2s
